pamphlet_excerpts: Hazards, First Aid & Safety: For more information about first aid, see the First Aid merit badge pamphlet (p. 26).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 2: Discuss with your counselor all the potential hazards stemming from your project (p. 26).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 3: Know the proper first aid for cuts, burns, and eye injuries (p. 26).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 4: To avoid minor cuts and scrapes, be sure you dress appropriately when working on your robot, for instance, jeans, boots, gloves (p. 26).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Treat minor cuts and scrapes by flushing the area with clean water for at least five minutes, or until all foreign matter appears to be washed away (p. 26).
Step 2 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Apply triple antibiotic ointment (if appropriate and if there are no known allergies) and cover with a dry, sterile bandage (p. 26).
Step 3 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Working under close supervision of a responsible adult and being careful when you work with materials that can cause burns will help prevent (p. 26).
Step 4 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): For chemical burns, it'simportant to quickly brush off as much of the chemical as possible using a gloved hand (p. 26).

options: A. Leave the battery connected so the servo motors hold torque while clearing the jammed gear teeth with bare fingers.

B. Wear ANSI Z87.1 safety glasses, disconnect the main battery before touching drive gears, brush off dry battery or flux chemicals with a gloved hand before flushing, and wash minor cuts with soap and running water for 5 minutes.
C. Pour water directly onto dry battery powder with bare hands and wrap the unwashed cut with electrical tape.
D. Remove safety glasses for a closer view of the spinning pinion gear while toggling the transmitter stick.

requirements.lead_text: Design, Build, Program, Test. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Design, Build, Program, Test. Do the following: (a) With your counselor's approval, choose a task for the robot or robotic subsystem that you plan to build. Include sensor feedback and programming in the task. Document this information in your robot engineering notebook. (b) Design your robot. The robot design should use sensors and programming and have at least 2 degrees of freedom. Document the design in your robot engineering notebook using drawings and a written description. (c) Build a robot or robotic subsystem of your original design to accomplish the task you chose for requirement 4(a). (d) Discuss with your counselor the programming options available for your robot. Then do ONE of the following: (1) Program your robot to perform the task you chose for your robot in 4(a). Include a sample of your program's source code in your robot engineering notebook. (2) Prepare a flowchart of the desired steps to program your robot for accomplishing the task in 4(a). Include procedures that show activities based on sensor inputs. Place this in your robot engineering notebook. (e) Test your robot and record the results in your robot engineering notebook. Include suggestions on how you could improve your robot, as well as pictures or sketches of your finished robot.
